summary:
SURFACE: the numeric levers of DOM and MEM. Enumerated from src/domains/levers.py and src/memory/levers.py by resolved declaration, not by eye: 54 levers total, of which 42 have an int or float (non-bool) default -- 22 DOM (8 int, 14 float) and 20 MEM (11 int, 9 float). 42 x 4 = 168 cells, every one run in a FRESH SUBPROCESS through a real spine.assemble.build(os.environ) and then driven into every DOM and MEM entry point that exists; plus a baseline cell and four spine.compose.compose() runs through the real composition root. Per-cell record in raw.json.

COUNTS PER OUTCOME (denominator 168):
  REFUSED_BY_NAME      19  -- every int lever at nan: `LeverError: MEM_TOPK='nan' is not a int`.
  REFUSED_BADLY        38  -- every int lever at inf and at -inf: uncaught OverflowError out of spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce, naming no lever, no value and no package.
  ACCEPTED_HARMFUL      2  -- MEM_QUOTA=0 (the whole store allocated with capacity 0, through the root) and MEM_OWNERS=0 (silently rewritten to 1; capacity 8192 -> 128).
  ACCEPTED_INERT        0.
  ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE   9  -- nine declared 0-sentinels, listed with their declaration sites in legitimate_specials.
  UNREACHABLE_TODAY   100  -- 69 float x {nan, inf, -inf} accepted-and-frozen with no live reader, plus 31 undeclared zeros likewise. The consuming entry point is a P4 stub in every one of the 100; compose() also halts at CAP.startup_refusals (row 29 of 39), which is why the cadence accessors were driven directly.
  CRASHED               0.
  (19+38+2+0+9+100+0 = 168.)

THE ONE-SENTENCE RESULT: the FAB_BALANCE hole is present in full on this surface and is un-armed only by the absence of bodies. Lever.coerce accepts nan/inf/-inf for all 23 float levers with no warning; not one of DOM's or MEM's 42 numeric levers declares a non-finite sentinel, so a finiteness refusal placed centrally in spine/lever.py would wrongly refuse ZERO configurations here. The int side is nearly right already and is one exception type from being right: nan is caught and refused by the lever's own name in exactly the tree's idiom, and inf escapes through the same `try` because OverflowError is not in `except (TypeError, ValueError)`. ZERO is the opposite case and must NOT be swept centrally: 9 zeros are declared sentinels with named declaration sites, and 18 more are endpoints of levers declared as 'fraction 0..1'.

NOTE ON GROUPING. The 168 cells are reported as 7 findings rather than 140, because they collapse into seven MECHANISMS and a ruling phase needs the mechanism, not 140 copies of one traceback. Every finding names the exact levers and values it covers and the covered counts reconcile exactly: 168 cells - 9 ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE - 19 REFUSED_BY_NAME (the good case, not a defect) = 140 defect cells, covered as 38 (finding 1, int x inf/-inf) + 1 (MEM_QUOTA=0) + 1 (MEM_OWNERS=0) + 1 (DOM_MANAGE_EVERY=0) + 69 (finding 5, float x nan/inf/-inf) + 5 (finding 6, the cull/fold brakes at 0) + 25 (finding 7, the remaining undeclared zeros) = 140. No cell is unaccounted for.

HARNESS (outside the repository, nothing in the tree was edited): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/sweep/ -- lv_enum.py (enumerates the 42 numeric levers off the resolved LeverSet subclasses), cell.py ENVNAME VALUE (one fresh process: sets the one env var, spine.assemble.build(os.environ), then every DOM and MEM entry point), run.py (drives all 168 cells, writes raw.json), comp2.py / comp4.py (spine.compose.compose(os.environ), the second with a spy wrapper on memory.api.open_store and domains.api.open_partition). Fresh subprocess per cell, so the assembly latch is never an issue.

findings.lever: spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce -- ALL 19 int levers of DOM+MEM
findings.detail: Lever.coerce does `v = int(float(raw))` for an int default inside `try: ... except (TypeError, ValueError)`. int(float('nan')) raises ValueError and IS caught, so nan comes back as the tree's own idiom -- `LeverError: DOM_CULL_STALE='nan' is not a int`. int(float('inf')) raises OverflowError, which is NOT in that except tuple, so it escapes spine/assemble.py::build uncaught. The operator's whole message is 'OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer'; the traceback's deepest frames are `assemble.py:1408 in <dictcomp>` and `lever.py:123 in coerce`, and NEITHER the env name nor the package prefix appears anywhere in it -- the prefix is the dictcomp variable `p`. One exception type away from a refusal that names itself, in the same function, on the same line. Affected (all 19, each at inf and at -inf): DOM_MANAGE_EVERY, DOM_SUSTAIN, DOM_RESERVOIR, DOM_CULL_ACT_MIN, DOM_CULL_STALE, DOM_GRACE, DOM_MIN_VISITS, DOM_RECUR_HORIZON, MEM_QUOTA, MEM_OWNERS, MEM_USE_DECAY_EVERY, MEM_KEY_WIN, MEM_KEY_DEPTH, MEM_REKEY_EVERY, MEM_PROBE_EVERY, MEM_PROBE_ROWS, MEM_TOPK, MEM_RECON_HID, MEM_RECON_TOK. Note this is the WHOLE non-finite story for int levers: nan is already refused by name, so the fix is a single `except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError)` or an explicit finiteness test.

$ MEM_TOPK=inf python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'src');import os;from spine import compose;compose.compose(os.environ)"
  File "/home/user/LLM-Test/src/spine/assemble.py", line 1408, in <dictcomp>
    configs = {p: sets[p].from_env(environ) for p in sorted(sets)}
  File "/home/user/LLM-Test/src/spine/lever.py", line 123, in coerce

OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
-- contrast, same function, same lever family:

[build] LeverError: DOM_CULL_STALE='nan' is not a int

findings.detail: MEM_QUOTA=0 is accepted by build and by the real composition root, and the whole editable store is allocated with ZERO rows. spine/assemble.py's d_capacity coupling computes `_owner_blocks(FAB.slots, MEM.owners) * int(MEM.quota)` = 64 * 0 = 0, and memory/api.py::open_store's own guard `if capacity != owners * quota` passes because 0 == 64 * 0. That guard exists specifically to stop 'one quantity, two answers' after the recorded 24x silent shrink (E7.40, 'no line in any log'); at quota=0 it is satisfied by an identity and the shrink is total rather than 24x. The store then reports `store.blocks: 64` -- sixty-four owner blocks that can hold nothing -- and `store.n_opened: 0`, and nothing raises, warns, or declares. MEM has NO `enabled` lever, so this is an undeclared off-switch for the entire mechanism goal B rests on. It is also a latent divide-by-zero: Store._block_of is `int(row) // self.quota`. Driven through spine.compose.compose(os.environ), which executes MEM.open_store at ASSEMBLY_ORDER's `store` row before it halts at CAP.startup_refusals, so this is the root's real behaviour today and not a direct-call artefact.

$ MEM_QUOTA=0 python comp4.py MEM_QUOTA 0        # spy wrapper around memory.api.open_store, then spine.compose.compose(os.environ)
  ROOT MEM.open_store -> capacity=0 quota=0 blocks=64 keys.shape=(0, 128) counters={'store.n_opened': 0, 'store.n_restored_entries': 0, 'store.n_restore_refused': 0, 'store.blocks': 64, 'store.census_slots': 8192}
  ROOT gate: Gate mem.key_depth: UNREACHABLE (0 vs 0) -- ...
  COMPOSE HALT: NotImplementedError CAP.startup_refusals: P4 (capacity) fills this in.
baseline for comparison (no env set):
  ROOT MEM.open_store -> capacity=8192 quota=128 blocks=64 keys.shape=(8192, 128)

findings.detail: MEM_OWNERS=0 is silently REWRITTEN to 1 by spine/assemble.py::_owner_blocks (`max(1, min(int(expert_slots), int(owner_buckets)))`), and the store's capacity falls from 8192 to 128 -- a 64x shrink -- with no refusal, no warning and no report line. The frozen Config still answers `mem.owners == 0` while `mem.d_owner_blocks == 1` and the built Store carries owners=1, so the printed configuration and the running one disagree about a number that sets the store's size. This is the exact shape the tree already refuses one package over: train/api.py::startup_refusals refuses RUN_EPOCHS=0 because `EPOCHS = max(1, _i(...))` 'SILENTLY REWROTE IT; a coercion at read time that makes a printed number a lie is the FAB_MIN_STEPS shape, so this is a refusal naming the lever, not a repair.' The identical max(1, ...) coercion sits in the spine's own coupling helper and is unrefused. Refusing it removes no configuration: memory/levers.py declares owners=1 as the single global store, so 1 already spells everything 0 could mean. Cost of leaving it: the 64x capacity change is exactly the class d_capacity was promoted to a wire to make visible.

DOM_MANAGE_EVERY=0 resolves, freezes, and DOM.manage_period returns Windows(0). The refusal that sits in that very function -- `if REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD and every < 0` -- is written strictly `< 0` and its own comment says 'ZERO IS NOT TOUCHED'. But 0 produces the SAME behaviour the negative refusal's message calls unacceptable: RUN.Cadences.due's stated contract is 'True at most once per `period` WINDOWS elapsed since this key last fired', so a body written to `step - last_fired >= period` is true on EVERY window at period 0 -- merge, then cull, then fold, every window -- while spine/derive.py::cadences_that_cannot_fire (live today) reports ('dom.manage', 0, 0), the line it prints for a gate that CANNOT FIRE. That is a printed verdict that is the inverse of the behaviour. It is UNREACHABLE_TODAY and not ACCEPTED_HARMFUL only because both consumers are stubs: domains/api.py::manage raises NotImplementedError and train/api.py::Cadences.due raises NotImplementedError. domains/levers.py states the intended meaning as an unimplemented PORT REQUIREMENT ('0 must mean NEVER, behind a guard at the read site... it is not implemented anywhere yet') and separately refuses to let 0 be read as the off-state (that is DOM_MANAGE). So 0 has no meaning in force -- it arms in the OPPOSITE direction from the one documented the moment P4 lands.

  periods: {'dom.manage': Windows(0), 'dom.rekey': Windows(0)}
  cadences_that_cannot_fire(run=Windows(506)): [('dom.manage', 0, 0), ('dom.rekey', 0, 0)]

findings.lever: ALL 23 float levers of DOM+MEM (see detail for the list)
findings.detail: spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce does a bare `float(raw)` for a float default. 'nan', 'inf' and '-inf' all parse, are stored, wired and frozen, and `cfg.<field>` hands back nan/inf/-inf. build() emits no warning. This is FAB_BALANCE=nan exactly, on 23 more levers -- the difference is that DOM and MEM have NO live reader of any float lever today, so nothing yet consumes the value: every consuming entry point (DOM.observe/rekey/manage/prior/on_retokenize/census, MEM.write/read/blend/maintain/judge/census/apply_domain_plan) raises NotImplementedError, and no Coupling in spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS reads a DOM or MEM float as a source. That is why this is UNREACHABLE_TODAY and not ACCEPTED_HARMFUL: the hole is latent, not absent, and it arms with P4. The predicates already WRITTEN in the frozen contracts that nan silently breaks, each a two-way switch whose two arms are both False at nan: memory/api.py::census `quota_arm` is "'reservoir' at src_share > 0, 'pressure_signal' at src_share == 0" -- at nan neither arm is selected and the report must name an arm; memory/api.py::blend 'blend_max == 0.0 is the clean retrieval-off null' -- at nan the null is not taken and the mix runs at weight nan, and blend's own docstring reasons that 'log(0) cannot arise while blend_max < 1', a comparison that is False at nan; domains/api.py::rekey 'radius_cap == 0 removes the guard and is a real arm' -- at nan the guard stays armed at a nan bound; domains/api.py::prior returns '(None, 0.0) when prior_blend == 0' -- at nan it returns a nan weight; memory/api.py::judge's 'judge_frac > 0' is False at nan. And blend/prior feed the output distribution, so a nan there is the FAB_BALANCE consequence (every gradient-carrying tensor non-finite) reached through MEM instead of FAB. `grep -rn 'isnan|isfinite' src/domains src/memory` prints nothing. Levers (each at nan, inf and -inf): DOM_SHIFT_DIST, DOM_SHIFT_Q, DOM_SHIFT_MULT, DOM_SPAWN_DIST, DOM_MARGIN, DOM_RADIUS_Q, DOM_RADIUS_MULT, DOM_RADIUS_CAP, DOM_MERGE_DIST, DOM_CULL_FRAC, DOM_DECAY, DOM_FOLD_MULT, DOM_PRIOR_BLEND, DOM_TOKC_DECAY, MEM_WRITE_GATE, MEM_WRITE_TARGET, MEM_USE_DECAY, MEM_SRC_SHARE, MEM_PROBATION_FRAC, MEM_PRESSURE_THRESH, MEM_BLEND_MAX, MEM_MATCH_FLOOR, MEM_JUDGE_FRAC. NO DOM OR MEM LEVER DECLARES A NON-FINITE SENTINEL ANYWHERE -- verified by reading all 42 declarations and by `grep -in 'infinit|no cap|uncapped'` over both levers.py and both api.py, which returns only prose about an 'unbounded fold'. A central finiteness rule in spine/lever.py would therefore wrongly refuse ZERO configurations on this surface.

findings.detail: The five conjuncts of the cull/fold rule that domains/levers.py calls 'THE LEVERS WITH THE SHARPEST CONTINUAL-LEARNING CONSEQUENCE' all accept 0, and 0 releases the brake rather than tightening it. grace=0 removes the minimum age before a newborn (or a restored, since grace re-arms on resume) domain may be culled; cull_stale=0 makes `now - last > 0` true for any domain not fed this very window; cull_act_min=0 makes `act < 0` false, which DISABLES that conjunct in the safe direction; min_visits=0 makes no domain a fold candidate. Nothing declares any of these zeros, and domains/api.py::manage -- the only reader -- is a P4 stub, so none of it executes today. The one that is documented in the negative is DOM_MIN_VISITS: domains/levers.py says the fold flag is 'KEPT AS AN EXPLICIT FLAG rather than expressed as min_visits=0, because a magic-zero off-switch is what produced SIG_WIN=0 meaning two different things on two paths -- one of the two confirmed fatal defects in the survey.' The declaration refuses to give 0 that meaning, and the environment hands it over anyway: DOM_MIN_VISITS=0 resolves and freezes, and once manage() exists it IS the fold off-switch the declaration says must not be spelled that way. Same for DOM_SUSTAIN=0 (a boundary declared with zero over-threshold windows, and the pending-signature average that sustain feeds into the assign query taken over an empty set) and DOM_RESERVOIR=0 (a per-domain sample of size 0, so the measured radius radius_q is a quantile of nothing and the reservoir replacement probability reservoir/size is 0).

  [DOM.manage] NotImplementedError: DOM.manage: P4 (domains) fills this in. The contract is frozen here; see docs/04_CONTRACT.md, section DOM.
(no wire moves; wires identical to baseline in all five cells)

findings.lever: DOM_SHIFT_DIST, DOM_SHIFT_Q, DOM_SHIFT_MULT, DOM_SPAWN_DIST, DOM_MARGIN, DOM_RADIUS_Q, DOM_RADIUS_MULT, DOM_MERGE_DIST, DOM_DECAY, DOM_FOLD_MULT, DOM_TOKC_DECAY, DOM_SUSTAIN, DOM_RESERVOIR, MEM_KEY_WIN, MEM_PROBE_ROWS, MEM_TOPK, MEM_RECON_HID, MEM_RECON_TOK, MEM_USE_DECAY, MEM_USE_DECAY_EVERY, MEM_WRITE_GATE, MEM_WRITE_TARGET, MEM_PROBATION_FRAC, MEM_PRESSURE_THRESH, MEM_MATCH_FLOOR
findings.detail: The remaining zeros with NO declared meaning and NO live reader. build accepts each, freezes it, and every consuming entry point raises NotImplementedError. Recorded so the ruling phase can see which zeros a central rule would newly refuse, and what each would do once P4 lands: MEM_KEY_WIN=0 keys the store off a zero-width slice of the model input (memory/levers.py: 'How many preceding input positions the encoder sees when it builds one memory key' -- at 0 there is nothing to encode, and the value is also written into the checkpoint at :5339 so a loader reproduces it); MEM_TOPK=0 makes `kk = min(self.topk, vi.numel())` zero, so every retrieval returns an empty neighbour set while n_reads still counts; MEM_RECON_HID=0 / MEM_RECON_TOK=0 build a degenerate Reconstructor(D, V, 0, 0) under verify='recon'; MEM_PROBE_ROWS=0 fires the probe cadence with zero query rows, which memory/api.py::maintain already anticipates as the honest 'armed-but-0' reading for empty probe_contexts; MEM_USE_DECAY=0 zeroes every retrieval counter at each decay interval (and memory/levers.py notes the arming test is `use_decay < 1.0`, which 0 satisfies); MEM_USE_DECAY_EVERY=0 decays on every write; MEM_WRITE_GATE=0 admits every candidate (surprise >= 0 always); MEM_PROBATION_FRAC=0 puts the never-retrieved region permanently over budget so eviction narrows to probation always; MEM_PRESSURE_THRESH=0 declares the store permanently short of room; DOM_SHIFT_DIST=0 trips a candidate boundary on every window; DOM_MERGE_DIST=0 merges nothing; DOM_DECAY=0 makes `act` a single-pass value rather than an EMA. MEM_WRITE_TARGET=0 is additionally inert on the shipped arm -- memory/levers.py declares it 'INERT UNDER write_mode="fixed"'.

  [MEM.write] NotImplementedError: MEM.write: P4 (memory) fills this in.
  [DOM.observe] NotImplementedError: DOM.observe: P4 (domains) fills this in.

legitimate_specials:
MEM_REKEY_EVERY=0 -- DISARM: the amortized re-encode is switched off. Declared twice: memory/api.py::maintain ('rekey_every == 0 DISARMS, behind a guard: the old tree documented 0 as the off switch and then divided by it') and memory/api.py::rekey_period ('ZERO IS NOT TOUCHED AND ITS DECLARED MEANING IS PRESERVED EXACTLY ... MEM_REKEY_EVERY=0 is the declared DISARM'). CAVEAT the ruling phase must keep: 0 is a declared sentinel for ONE of this lever's two readers. rekey_period returns Windows(0) and the spine's 'dom.rekey' gate goes through RUN.Cadences.due, which by its own contract fires on every window at period 0 -- the same two-mechanisms-disagree hazard the negative refusal three lines below it exists to prevent. Measured: cadences_that_cannot_fire(Windows(506), {'dom.rekey': Windows(0)}) -> [('dom.rekey', 0, 0)], i.e. 'cannot fire'. Refuse 0 here and the declared DISARM is lost; leave it and the second reader is unguarded.
MEM_PROBE_EVERY=0 -- the training-time read probe is off. Declared in memory/levers.py::probe_every: 'Setting this to 0 disarms every retrieval-based rule above; the report must say so.' A central refusal of 0 would remove the only way to ask for the pre-probe baseline the whole evict='usage'/'lru' measurement is scored against.
MEM_KEY_DEPTH=0 -- 'the full stack'. Declared in the help text itself: 'Cap the transformer depth used for the memory key path only; 0 = the full stack.' It is also the DEFAULT, and it is read live today by memory/api.py::open_store to build the mem.key_depth Gate. Refusing 0 would refuse the shipped configuration.
MEM_BLEND_MAX=0 -- retrieval contributes nothing; the clean retrieval-off null. Declared in the help text ('0 turns retrieval's contribution off') and again in memory/api.py::blend ('blend_max == 0.0 is the clean retrieval-off null and returns model_probs untouched') and in memory/levers.py ('blend_max=0 is also the clean retrieval-off null the memory arm needs as its baseline').
MEM_SRC_SHARE=0 -- selects D3's superseded 'pressure is a signal, not a wall' arm. Declared in memory/levers.py ('the arm src_share=0 -- memory.py:365 returns the candidate set untouched at <= 0.0, so 0 genuinely disarms and does not crash') and in memory/api.py::census, whose reported quota_arm is "'reservoir' at src_share > 0, 'pressure_signal' at src_share == 0". Refusing 0 deletes one of two declared arms.
MEM_JUDGE_FRAC=0 -- 'stale-selfcon only': re-score nothing beyond the entries written since the last pass. Declared in the help text ('0.0 re-scores nothing') and at length in the declaration comment ('DEFAULT 0.0 = THE RE-SCORE IS OFF, and both arms are reachable from the environment'). It is the DEFAULT.
DOM_RADIUS_CAP=0 -- removes the Voronoi guard. Declared in the help text ('0 removes the guard'), in the declaration comment ('0 is a REAL arm precisely because the table shows the guard inert in the healthy case', with the measured cap sweep beside it) and in domains/api.py::rekey ('radius_cap == 0 removes the guard and is a real arm').
DOM_PRIOR_BLEND=0 -- the honest off-switch for the per-domain token prior, on BOTH of its jobs. Declared in domains/levers.py ('0.0 disables the accounting entirely and costs nothing, which is the honest off-switch') and in domains/api.py::prior ('Returns (probs, weight), or (None, 0.0) when prior_blend == 0').
DOM_CULL_FRAC=0 -- an empty cull budget: int(0 * n) == 0 domains considered per pass. Declared only WEAKLY, and the ruling phase should know how weakly: there is no sentence in the declaration, but domains/api.py::manage's DID IT FIRE list names a dedicated counter `n_cull_budget_zero`, so the state is anticipated by name. Given that this lever's entire comment is the history of a max(1, ...) floor that ratcheted a population to one domain, a zero budget is the safe direction and refusing it would remove the strongest available brake on the cull.
THE CLASS A CENTRAL 'REFUSE 0' RULE WOULD BREAK BEYOND THOSE NINE: 14 of the 23 floats here are declared U.FRACTION 'fraction 0..1' and 0 is an ENDPOINT OF THE DECLARED RANGE, not an out-of-range value -- DOM_SHIFT_DIST, DOM_SHIFT_Q, DOM_SPAWN_DIST, DOM_MARGIN, DOM_RADIUS_Q, DOM_MERGE_DIST, DOM_CULL_FRAC, DOM_DECAY, DOM_PRIOR_BLEND, DOM_TOKC_DECAY, MEM_WRITE_TARGET, MEM_USE_DECAY, MEM_SRC_SHARE, MEM_PROBATION_FRAC, MEM_PRESSURE_THRESH, MEM_BLEND_MAX, MEM_MATCH_FLOOR, MEM_JUDGE_FRAC (plus MEM_WRITE_GATE at U.PROBABILITY). A rule over 0 belongs per-lever; a rule over NON-FINITE values does not, and see the next line.
NO NON-FINITE SENTINEL EXISTS ON THIS SURFACE. All 42 declarations were read and `grep -in 'infinit|inf)|no cap|uncapped|unbounded'` over src/domains/levers.py, src/memory/levers.py, src/domains/api.py and src/memory/api.py returns only three prose hits about an 'unbounded' population or fold. Not one lever spells 'no cap' as inf; where a lever HAS an off-arm it is spelled 0 (DOM_RADIUS_CAP) or a flag (DOM_MANAGE, DOM_FOLD, DOM_ENABLED). A finiteness refusal placed in spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce would wrongly refuse exactly ZERO of the 42 numeric levers of DOM and MEM.
MEM_OWNERS=1 (not swept, stated for contrast) -- 'the single global store', declared in the help text. It is what makes MEM_OWNERS=0's silent fold to 1 costless to refuse: 1 already spells it.
